```{r}
#SECTION ONE: INSTALL AND LOAD packages

# Define a helper function `quiet_library`:
# - Takes a package name as input
# - Installs the package if it is not already installed
# - Loads the package while suppressing warnings and messages
quiet_library <- function(pkg) {
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings({
    if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(pkg, quiet = TRUE) # Install without messages
    }
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE) # Load silently
  }))
}

# Load required packages (install if missing)
quiet_library("tidyverse")   # for data wrangling and visualization
quiet_library("carData")     # companion datasets for the 'car' package
quiet_library("gtsummary")   # for creating publication-ready summary tables
quiet_library("flextable")   # for customizable tables in reports
quiet_library("officer")     # needed for flextable advanced customization

```

```{r}
#=-=============SECTION THREE: LOOK AT THE DATA=================

#Get a list of all variables in the dataset using colnames
names(msleepdata)

msleepdata$sleep_total #total amount of sleep in hours

#Use summary to get a relevant statistical summary for a variable
summary(msleepdata$vore) #carnivore,herbivore etc

summary (msleepdata$brainwt)

summary(msleepdata)


#The distribution of observations across mammalian foraging types
table(msleepdata$vore)

#To see investigate the conservation status by vore type 

#We start by creating a table
table(msleepdata$conservation, msleepdata$vore)

#Then we can look at the proportions
proportions(table(msleepdata$conservation, msleepdata$vore))

# Show the proportion of each conservation status for each vore type (Row wise proportions)
# e.g. Critically Endagered Carnivore: 50%, Domesticated Herbivore: 70%
proportions(table(msleepdata$conservation, msleepdata$vore),margin = 1)

# Columnwise proportions
proportions(table(msleepdata$vore, msleepdata$conservation),margin = 1)


#Using the gtsummary package using pipes to create a prettier version of the table
msleepdata |>
  select(conservation, vore) |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary()

#Showing proportions
msleepdata |>
  select(conservation, vore) |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)") # Show counts and proportions
  )

#Using flextable to create a version that can be saved to a file
msleepdata |>
  select(conservation, vore) |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    by = conservation, # Group by conservation
    statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")) |> # Show counts and proportions 
  gtsummary::as_flex_table() |> # Convert the table to a format that can be exported
  flextable::save_as_docx(path = "my_table.docx") # Save the file
#By default this will be saved in your default working directory
#To check where this is in the Console pane enter the command getwd()




# Create styled flextable
msleepdata |>
  select(conservation, vore) |>
  tbl_summary(
    by = vore, # group by vore type
    statistic = list(all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")
  ) |>
  as_flex_table() |>
  theme_vanilla() |> # start with a clean theme
  border_outer(part = "all", border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 2)) |> # thick outer border
  border_inner_h(part = "all", border = fp_border(color = "darkblue", width = 1)) |> # horizontal lines
  border_inner_v(part = "all", border = fp_border(color = "darkblue", width = 1)) |> # vertical lines
  color(color = "white", part = "header") |> # white text in header
  bg(bg = "darkblue", part = "header") |> # dark blue header background
  bold(part = "header") |> # bold header text
  autofit() |> 
  save_as_docx(path = "my_fancy_table.docx")
#By default this will be saved in your default working directory
#To check where this is in the Console pane enter the command getwd()
```

```{r}
# 📊 2. Using prop.table()
# prop.table() converts a frequency table into proportions (i.e., percentages).

# Overall proportions
prop.table(table(msleepdata$vore))

# Proportion by row or column
prop.table(table(msleepdata$vore, msleepdata$conservation), margin = 1)  # by vore
prop.table(table(msleepdata$vore, msleepdata$conservation), margin = 2)  # by conservation
```



```{r}
# 📋 3. Using gtsummary::tbl_summary()
# 
# This produces publication-quality summary tables — especially great for reports.
# Install if needed
# install.packages("gtsummary")
library(gtsummary)

# Summary of categorical variables
msleepdata %>%
  select(vore, conservation) %>%
  tbl_summary()


# you cna add continuous variables too
# This gives you mean, median, and IQR of sleep_total grouped by diet type (vore).
msleepdata %>%
  select(vore, sleep_total) %>%
  tbl_summary(by = vore)



```


```{r}
#🪶 4. Using flextable
#To turn a simple table into a nicely formatted one for Word, PowerPoint, or HTML reports:
  
# install.packages("flextable")
library(flextable)

# Create a table of vore vs conservation
tab <- table(msleepdata$vore, msleepdata$conservation)

# Convert it to a flextable
ft <- flextable::qflextable(as.data.frame(tab))
ft

#or directly
ft <- flextable(as.data.frame(tab))
ft <- autofit(ft)
ft


```


```{r}
<!-- 🧠 Summary of Each Approach -->

  
  | Function                   | Purpose             | Output Type                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `table()`                  | Counts              | Basic R table                         |
| `prop.table()`             | Percentages         | Numeric matrix                        |
| `gtsummary::tbl_summary()` | Descriptive summary | Publication-style table               |
| `flextable()`              | Nicely formatted    | Report-ready table (Word, HTML, etc.) |

```

```{R}
#Mode
#R doesn't have a built in function to compute the mode but there is a simple function which you can write and include in your code  that will do it for you")

getmode <- function(v)
{
  uniqv <- unique(v)
  uniqv[which.max(tabulate(match(v,uniqv)))]
}


#Use the function to get the mode of total sleep hours
getmode(msleepdata$sleep_total)

#---------------------------------
```


```{r}

# >>>>>> Central Tendency functions- <<<< below -- next 5 below
# 1️⃣ Mean
# 
# The mean (average) is calculated using mean().
# Mean total sleep (in hours)
mean(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# 2️⃣ Median
# 
# The median is the middle value when data are sorted.

median(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# 3️⃣ Mode
# 
# R doesn’t have a built-in mode function, but you can find the most frequent value using:


# Simple custom mode function
mode_func <- function(x) {
  ux <- na.omit(unique(x))
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# Example: mode of vore (diet type)
mode_func(msleepdata$vore)
```
```{r}
# 4️⃣ Summary of a Variable
# 
# You can quickly view several central tendency stats at once with:

summary(msleepdata$sleep_total)
```
```{r}
# 5️⃣ Grouped Central Tendency (using tidyverse)
# 
# You can calculate central tendency by category — e.g., average sleep by diet type (vore):

library(dplyr)

msleepdata %>%
  group_by(vore) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_sleep = mean(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_sleep = median(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = n()
  )
```

```{r}
# 📊 Dispersion Functions in R
# 
# Dispersion (or variability) measures how consistent or variable your data values are.
# 
# Common dispersion measures:
# 
# Range
# 
# Variance
# 
# Standard deviation
# 
# Interquartile range (IQR)
# 
# Minimum / Maximum

```




```{r}
1️⃣ Range

The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values.

# Range of total sleep
range(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)

# Difference between max and min
diff(range(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
2️⃣ Variance

Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean.

var(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)
```


```{r}
3️⃣ Standard Deviation

Standard deviation is the square root of variance, measuring spread in the same units as your data.

sd(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```
4️⃣ Interquartile Range (IQR)

IQR = difference between the 75th percentile (Q3) and 25th percentile (Q1).
It’s a measure of the middle 50% of your data

IQR(msleepdata$sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
5️⃣ Five-Number Summary

You can get a quick summary of spread with summary():

summary(msleepdata$sleep_total)
```


```{r}


6️⃣ Grouped Dispersion (using tidyverse)

You can calculate measures of spread by group (e.g., by diet type):

library(dplyr)

msleepdata %>%
  group_by(vore) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_sleep = mean(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_sleep = sd(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    var_sleep = var(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_sleep = IQR(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE),
    range_sleep = diff(range(sleep_total, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
```

```{r}

| Function        | Measure                 | Description                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `range()`       | Range                   | Min and max values             |
| `diff(range())` | Range width             | Max − Min                      |
| `var()`         | Variance                | Average squared deviation      |
| `sd()`          | Standard deviation      | Square root of variance        |
| `IQR()`         | Interquartile range     | Q3 − Q1                        |
| `summary()`     | Quick descriptive stats | Min, Q1, Median, Mean, Q3, Max |

```
